$comment: TF-C121 (D-FFI-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-LINK-NAME) — the RUNTIME witness for the per-target link BASE name, and for the one assertion whose absence let a silent misbinding corrupt real data. Darwin reaches its modern 64-bit-inode ABI through `$INODE64` asm-label aliases on x86_64 and through the PLAIN names on arm64 (sys/cdefs.h: __DARWIN_ONLY_64_BIT_INO_T is 0 / 1); DSS declared the plain names everywhere, so an x86_64-Darwin build bound the LEGACY 32-bit-inode implementations while compiling the MODERN 144-byte `struct stat`. The legacy callee writes 120 bytes, st_size is read at 96 and written at 72 ⇒ fstat reports 0 ⇒ sqlite calls every database 'malformed'. It never failed loud: a descriptor SHADOWS the SDK header entirely (src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp — Descriptor beats Source), so the platform's own asm label never participates, and libSystem exports BOTH spellings so the plain import resolves. ★ WHY THIS EXISTS ALONGSIDE shipped_sys_stat: that example already calls fstat and PASSED throughout the bug, because its assertion is `st.st_size >= 0` — which a zero satisfies. THE VALUE WAS NEVER CHECKED. This one writes 4141 known bytes and demands exactly 4141 back three times (fstat by fd, stat by path, lstat by path), then finds the file it just created by readdir name-compare (the LATENT half: modern `struct dirent` puts d_name at 21, the legacy one at 8, so a wrong binding reads garbage and never matches). ★ THE ARMS ARE A CONTROL SET, not a coverage list: macho64-x86_64 is the arm the `linkName` variants fire on; macho64-arm64 is the MATCHED CONTROL where no variant matches and the plain names are already correct (it passed before this cycle and must still pass); the two elf arms are the second control — no Linux symbol carries a link name at all, so they exercise the DEFAULT path through the SAME single decoration rule, which is the property `linkName` was designed around. pe is absent because sys/stat.json gates the POSIX fstat/lstat/stat rows [elf,macho] and windirent is a separate axis. ★ THE x86_64-DARWIN ARM DECLARES NO EMULATOR and that is honest, not an omission: no arm anywhere in the corpus declares one for (arch=x86_64, runOn=darwin), so `lintDeclaredEmulators` stays silent for the pair; on an Intel Mac it runs natively, on Apple Silicon Rosetta 2 translates it transparently, and on every non-Darwin host it is compile-only — which still proves the descriptor resolves and the import is named. HERMETIC: the only file created is /tmp/dss_c121_inode64_<pid>.bin, unlinked before exit; <pid> makes it collision-free, and /tmp is the same directory the readdir scan walks, so the entry the scan must find is one this process just created rather than a guessed fixture. Exit 42 = st_size AS REPORTED (4141/101 = 41) + the readdir hit (1) — the 4141 is never a literal in the sum, so a binding that answers 0 yields 1 and cannot fold to 42. Guard codes 11..22 name the exact call that failed. RED-ON-DISABLE: drop the `linkName` key from sys/stat.json's fstat row → the macho64-x86_64 arm returns 14; drop it from dirent.json's readdir row → that arm returns 22; both stay green on arm64-macho and on elf, which is what makes a failure attributable to the arch rather than to the program. The release arm re-runs every call under the full optimizer.
